note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  Acute central chest pressure radiating to left arm/shoulder with shortness of breath, diaphoresis, and nausea started a few hours ago while gardening; symptoms ongoing at rest. Risk factors: male in ~60s, hypertension, smoker (10 cigarettes/day for 15 years), overweight/sedentary lifestyle, family history of premature heart disease.
- Relevant family medical history:  Father died of myocardial infarction around age ~60; mother with unspecified “heart problems.”
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  No regular medications recorded. Allergy: aspirin—causes swelling (mild allergic reaction); no other allergies mentioned.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Sedentary; overweight. Diet not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Tobacco: ~10 cigarettes/day for 15 years. Alcohol: ~7–8 pints of beer/week. Other substances: Not recorded.
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Not recorded.
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Lives alone. Works as a restaurant owner (sushi shop). Caring responsibilities not recorded.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (telehealth; no vitals obtained).
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Overweight by patient report; exact measurements not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: First-episode, ongoing central chest pressure with left arm radiation, dyspnea, diaphoresis, and nausea at rest in a man with hypertension, tobacco use, overweight, sedentary lifestyle, and strong family history of premature cardiac disease. No vitals or ECG available at time of call.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx and transcript):
  - Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina/NSTEMI/STEMI): High suspicion given classic ischemic symptoms at rest and multiple risk factors.
  - Aortic dissection: Considered due to hypertension and acute chest pain; less typical (pressure quality, left arm radiation, no back pain/neuro deficits reported).
  - Pulmonary embolism: Less likely; pain not pleuritic and has classic ischemic radiation.
- Working diagnosis: Suspected acute coronary syndrome.
- Management priorities: Immediate emergency assessment with ECG and cardiac biomarkers; communicate aspirin allergy (swelling) to EMS/hospital—clinician noted aspirin may still be considered despite allergy depending on severity and clinical need.

Management Plan

- Immediate actions: Ambulance called; clinician remained on the line. Patient instructed to keep front door open for access. EMS to perform ECG on arrival and transport based on findings.
- Follow-up: Hospital evaluation for ACS rule-in/rule-out and management as indicated.
- Patient education: Informed that symptoms may represent a heart attack and the urgency of evaluation. Advised to inform hospital staff of aspirin allergy details.
- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina/NSTEMI/STEMI) – Likelihood: High. Justification: Classic pressure-like chest pain with left arm radiation, diaphoresis, nausea, and dyspnea at rest; major risk factors and strong family history.
- Aortic dissection – Likelihood: Low-Moderate. Justification: Acute chest pain in a hypertensive patient; lacks tearing quality/back radiation or neurologic signs.
- Pulmonary embolism – Likelihood: Low. Justification: Dyspnea present but pain not pleuritic; arm radiation and autonomic symptoms favor cardiac ischemia; no DVT risk factors elicited.

Quality checks
- Missing expected elements: Vitals (BP, pulse), BMI/waist, comprehensive medication list, immunization review, mental health screening, hearing/vision screening, oral/dental exam, urinalysis, fasting glucose and lipid profile, other preventive screenings (STI screen, cancer screening as applicable), detailed alcohol risk screening, diet assessment.
- Internal contradictions: Age references varied; DOB given as 1958 (implies mid-60s). Clinician/patient also referenced “around sixty.” No conflict with DDx noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear telehealth history focused on acute symptoms; limited by absence of physical exam and vitals.
